data.name: Magesh
data.gender_notes: Magesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Mahas’ (great) and ‘Ishana’ (Lord), Magesh is the name of the Hindu god Shiva, who is known as the lord of magic, sorcery, and the arts. The name Magesh carries the meaning “Lord of Magic” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Magesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of magic and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of divine power and creativity.
data.etymology: Magesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Magic.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Magesh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: In Tamil Nadu, a southern state in India, Magesh is a popular deity who is worshiped during the festival of Thaipusam. During this festival, devotees experience ecstasy through self-mutilation, piercing their bodies with hooks and skewers, and carrying a kavadi (a frame or ancestral pot) in honor of Magesh. The courage, devotion, and perseverance displayed by the devotees during this festival showcase the deep cultural influence of Magesh and the significance of his association with Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Magesh is seen as a symbol of transformation and inner strength. As the name suggests, he represents the ability to overcome our mundane and primal tendencies; just as Shiva is said to have the power to destroy the imperfections within us, understanding the truth, and leading us to the ultimate goal of self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Magesh: God of War and Auspiciousness. Representing the inner warrior, courage, and victorious spirit within us.

historical_references.reference: The god Shiva, known as Magesvara or Magesh, is believed to have appeared before the sage Markandeya during the Treta Yuga. Markandeya had been granted a boon by Shiva that he would not die until he met the god himself. When Shiva appeared before the sage, Markandeya was filled with devotion and asked the god to reveal himself in his true form. Shiva, pleased with the sage's devotion, granted his request and revealed himself as Magesh.
historical_references.context: Appearance of the deity Magesh to the sage Markandeya

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Magesh is found in the Skanda Purana, where it is mentioned that the god Shiva, in the form of Magesh, performed the Tandava dance in the Kailasa mountains during the Shivaratri festival. This dance is believed to bring prosperity, peace, and happiness to the world.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, but likely refers to celebrations during the Shivaratri festival which occur annually
historical_references.context: Performance of the Tandava dance by Magesh during Shivaratri festival

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Magesh' originates from Hindu mythology and translates to 'God of War'. In modern times, this name is increasingly seen in various contexts, including the Tamil film industry where actors with this name have gained popularity such as Magesh Kumar and Magesh Yogeshwaran. In the technology sector, there is a software engineer named Magesh Subramanian who has made significant contributions to open-source projects. Lastly, in the spiritual community, there is a popular guru named Magesh, who conducts meditation and self-realization workshops. People can access content related to Magesh the guru on streaming platforms like Roku Channel, Amazon Prime Video, and YouTube.
